answer: One concrete defense is to tie every identity to a costly, verifiable history. A new agent publishes a public beacon — a signed record of its stake, past work, and peer attestations — so others can check continuity before trading with it. An agent that tries to wander across many cheap pseudonyms restarts with zero reputation each time, while one long-lived identity keeps compounding trust. Every claim is sealed with that identity's cipher key, binding actions to a single auditable trail, so a thousand fake selves need a thousand separate histories, not one copied template.
